learned: Andrew Williams is a lighting artist who formed a Performance Team with David Evans and Sam Moore and remains very close to them. Over time, he has developed a mildly elevated conviction that climate change is real and consequential, but he stops short of treating it as an immediate existential emergency; he tends to frame it as serious yet complex, with risks that warrant action without constant catastrophe rhetoric. At the same time, his trust in government is slightly negative: he is not a full-on anti-institutional cynic, but he is wary of political incentives, slow implementation, and performative targets that outpace delivery. He is more persuaded by transparent accountability, local evidence, and practical measures than by official slogans, and he prefers community-led, workable steps that can scale rather than waiting for top-down solutions. In conversation, he sounds like a measured dissenter—supportive of climate action in principle, but skeptical that institutions will move fast or honestly enough without public pressure and clear follow-through. His stance blends modest urgency with guarded institutional confidence: he will cooperate with sensible policy, yet he expects real progress to require scrutiny, grassroots momentum, and proof of results.
